summary: The NATIVE mapping and the Go wrapper make cl_http_utility=>decode_base64 compile, and the Base64 step matches Node for padded, unpadded, URL-safe, mid-string '=' and junk-character inputs. The hand-written UTF-8 validator does not match Node's (WHATWG) decoding in two ways. It passes encoded surrogates through as raw invalid bytes, and it emits one U+FFFD per byte for truncated multibyte sequences where Node emits one per maximal subpart. Both are in the acceptance criteria and are covered by the hidden nodeutf8 tests, which fail.

findings.claim: The 3-byte branch rejects overlongs only for E0 and never rejects UTF-16 surrogates (ED followed by A0..BF). ED A0 80 is therefore accepted as valid and copied verbatim, so Decode returns invalid UTF-8. Node returns three U+FFFD. Through ABAP, strlen of the result is 1 instead of 3.
findings.repro: Decode("7aCA") returns "\xed\xa0\x80"; node -e 'console.log(JSON.stringify(Buffer.from("7aCA","base64").toString()))' prints "\ufffd\ufffd\ufffd". In an osgo ABAP Unit case, strlen( cl_http_utility=>decode_base64( '7aCA' ) ) gives 1, expected 3.

findings.claim: On any invalid sequence the decoder emits one U+FFFD and skips exactly one byte. Node/WHATWG replaces each maximal subpart (a valid prefix of a sequence) with a single U+FFFD. Because of this, incomplete sequences produce too many replacement characters: E8 80 gives 2 instead of 1, F0 9F 98 gives 3 instead of 1, and F0 9F 98 41 gives 3 U+FFFD plus 'A' instead of 1 plus 'A'.
findings.repro: Decode("6IA=") = "\ufffd\ufffd" vs Node "\ufffd"; Decode("8J+Y") = 3x U+FFFD vs Node 1x; Decode("8J+YQQ==") = "\ufffd\ufffd\ufffdA" vs Node "\ufffdA"

findings.claim: The code re-implements UTF-8 validation by hand and returns a rune value it never computes (always 0). An algorithm that tracks the expected continuation-byte range for each lead byte (the WHATWG UTF-8 decoder) would fix both defects above in fewer lines. The unit tests only use single-byte truncations, which is why they never caught the maximal-subpart difference.
The new ABAP fixture is not referenced by any test or runner (grep for b64text/B64TEXT finds nothing), so the ABAP path the change adds has no automated coverage in the repository.
